followup_reviews.Research finding: Serbia’s successive passenger-entry rules are supported. The selected phase remains a formal policy period and is not relabelled operational. Initial exemptions for citizens, residents and diplomats; tightening to passenger closure from 20 March with freight trucks excepted; conditional citizen/resident readmission on 12 May. Other foreigners still needed PCR and commission permission at that point. The initial announcement was 15 March. The selected 20 March–12 May phase yields a 53-day policy-date difference. Later 22 May formal easing is separately described and does not alter that selected endpoint or prove universal first traffic. Human disease control is supported by government statements, including concerns about return flows. The code does not imply all possible reasons were identified. Three official Serbian pages were directly read. The 22 May context was checked against TSG’s cited legal analysis and an indexed Bosnian border-police notice; the latter direct page returned 502. The phase remains unlocated. The Kosovo boundary is explicitly disputed and its actual implementation was not freshly mapped. Neighbour country labels do not certify every crossing’s operation.
